findings.issue: The round-1 fix for the invisible typed-confirmation gate switches off BOTH buttons of every danger dialog, not just the confirm. WButton renders inside `<span class="w-tooltip-wrap">` whenever it has a Tooltip (WDialog always passes one), so inside `.w-dialog-actions` each button is the first child of its OWN wrapper and `.w-btn:first-child` matches the confirm AND the cancel. Measured live on the running host, revoke dialog of A07 before typing: [{"label":"إلغاء الجهاز","pe":"none","op":"0.55"},{"label":"العودة","pe":"none","op":"0.55","cur":"not-allowed"}] — identical in the A04 numbering dialog («تغيير صيغة الترقيم؟»). Both buttons are visibly dimmed in the screenshot. Because AdminConfirmDialog passes `CloseOnScrimClick="@(!Danger)"`, the scrim is dead too, so a person who opened «إلغاء الجهاز» by mistake is left with the way back greyed out and only the X or Esc working. The A07 preview shows exactly the opposite: the confirm dimmed and «تراجع» at full brightness. The bUnit test added for this (AdminAreaScreenTests.DangerDialog_KeepsItsMainButtonSwitchedOffUntilTheWordMatches) only asserts the marker class, which a CSS-less bUnit host can never catch.
findings.fix: Scope the rule to the confirm action only — the confirm is the first CHILD of `.w-dialog-actions`, so write `.w-dialog--confirm-locked .w-dialog-actions > :first-child .w-btn { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: .55; pointer-events: none; }` — then re-measure both buttons on the running host and confirm «العودة» reports pointerEvents auto / opacity 1 while the confirm is off. Better: add a `ConfirmDisabled` parameter to WDialog (Wakeel.Design owner) and delete the rule. Add a host or unit check that asserts the cancel button stays live while the dialog is locked.

findings.issue: The square-crop focus slider commits on every `@oninput`. `OnFocusChanged` calls `ApplyLogo`, which re-decodes and re-encodes the picture, writes it to admin.db through `Org.SaveLogo`, re-reads the identity and raises `Toasts.Show(AdminAr.Organisation.Logo.Saved)`. Reproduced on the running host after uploading a 600×300 PNG: firing 21 slider steps left 21 stacked «حُفظ الشعار.» toasts running the full height of the screen and covering the page actions and the logo/numbering cards, plus 21 PNG decode+crop+encode cycles and 21 database writes. A real mouse drag produces far more.
findings.fix: Re-crop the preview only on `@oninput` (set `_focus`, recompute `_logoPreview` from the cropper, do not touch the database), and commit — `Org.SaveLogo` plus the one toast — on `@onchange`, when the person lets the slider go. Verify on the host that a full drag leaves exactly one toast.

findings.issue: The offices rail is a hand-rolled selectable list: a bare `<ul class="a06-list"><li><button class="a06-office">` whose page stylesheet defines its own padding, border, border-radius, hover surface and a selected state painted with `--w-primary-soft` / `--w-primary-border` / `--w-primary`. The owner's design-consistency rule forbids hand-rolled lists inside a page, and a shared component now exists for exactly this shape (WTree, used with one level, or WTable). This is the same class of deviation as the reserved A05 tree but is not covered by that ruling. The builder's note «No page stylesheet defines a surface, border, radius or semantic colour any more» is not accurate: `.a06-office`, `.a04-template`, `.a04-example` and `.a07-subject` all still paint a surface + border + radius in page CSS.
findings.fix: Move the offices rail onto the shared component (WTree with a single level, or a WList if one is added to Wakeel.Design with css + gallery entry + bUnit test), and delete `.a06-office*` from the page stylesheet; hand the same pass the three remaining page-painted surfaces (`.a04-template`, `.a04-example`, `.a07-subject`) so page CSS only arranges components. If it is to be deferred, it belongs in the same design-consistency package as the A05 tree and must be recorded there explicitly.

findings.issue: KNOWN, RESERVED — recorded once, not a blocker. A05's tree is still the hand-rolled AdminStructureNode. Measured on the running host the indent is 18px a level (`padding-inline-start: 8 + Depth*18`), so on screen the four layers read as an almost flat list: the level chips of هيئة/دائرة/قسم/وحدة sit at x≈1264/1246/1228/1210.
findings.fix: Leave for the shared-WTree design-consistency package as ruled; when it lands, move the tree pane and the office rail of A06 with it.

findings.issue: Arabic gender agreement — the same class of defect as the round-1 «جهازان نشطة» low. `Log.Added/Updated/Disabled/Deleted` always use a feminine verb («أُضيفت», «عُدّلت», «أُوقفت», «حُذفت») while `LevelName` returns a masculine noun for one of the four layers («قسم»). Seen on the running host's A03 pending-changes list: «أُضيفت قسم «قسم الصادر والوارد».» beside the correct «أُضيفت دائرة «دائرة الشؤون الإدارية».» The same strings go into the operations log A11 will show.
findings.fix: Give `LevelName` a companion that returns the matching verb form per level (هيئة/دائرة/وحدة feminine, قسم masculine) and use it in all four Log helpers; add a test asserting «أُضيف قسم …» and «أُضيفت دائرة …».

findings.issue: A07's `Reload()` calls `DeviceKeys.BuildRevocationList()` on every page open, every office change and after every action. That opens the organisation identity (`_org.OpenOrgIdentity()`, i.e. unseals the org signing key) and signs a brand-new list each time, for display only. Two consequences: the organisation private key is unsealed far more often than any signing actually requires, and the card's «وُقّعت في …» line always shows the current moment instead of when the list was really issued and written to keys/revocations.json.
findings.fix: For display, read the list that was written out (`ReadSavedRevocationList()`), falling back to building one only when no file exists; keep `BuildRevocationList()` for the moment a device is actually revoked (and for A08's export).

findings.issue: The display query still carries `COALESCE(a.role, 'manager')` and `COALESCE(a.employee_no, 1)`, so a device whose account row is missing — a registration that stopped between its two writes — is shown to the administrator on A06 and A07 as «مدير المكتب · الموظف ١». The round-1 fix removed exactly this default from `ReadDeviceRow` (where it would have been signed into a certificate) but left the screens telling the person the same untrue, most-privileged thing.
findings.fix: Return the row without a role/employee when the LEFT JOIN finds no account (nullable fields on AdminDevice, or skip it) and have A06/A07 draw a «سجل ناقص» state for it, so a half-made device is visible as half made instead of as a manager.

findings.issue: Immediately after «إصدار المفتاح» is pressed for the very first time, the key card reads «آخر تدوير ⁦17/09/2026⁩» — last ROTATION — although the key has never been rotated. Observed on the running host right after the first issue (key_version 1).
findings.fix: Choose the wording by version: «أُصدر في …» when `_key.Version == 1`, «آخر تدوير …» from the second version onwards.

findings.issue: Within one card the value is drawn «0» in Latin figures and the line under it «من ١ · مكتب بانتظار ملف الإعداد» in Arabic-Indic, so the same card speaks in two figure systems. Observed on the running host after admin-2's data existed. (The «1 / 1 / 1» structure KPI was expressly accepted in round 1; this one mixes the two inside a single card.)
findings.fix: Draw the office KPI value with `AdminAr.Digits` so it matches the «من ١» beneath it, or draw both sides in the same system.

findings.issue: The 4 MB cap is applied to the compressed file only; `word/document.xml` (and every header and footer) is then handed straight to `XDocument.Load` with no limit on the decompressed size, so a crafted 4 MB docx can expand to hundreds of megabytes in the window's memory. The person chooses the file themselves, so this is a robustness rather than a trust problem — and the XML side is otherwise sound (XDocument.Load prohibits DTDs by default, no macro is executed, mc:Fallback is skipped).
findings.fix: Read each part through a length-limited stream (e.g. wrap `entry.Open()` and abort past a few megabytes, or check `entry.Length` before opening) and return `LetterTemplateReport.Unreadable` when a part is past the limit.

notes:
BUILD AND TESTS — all four commands run exactly as given, full output read. `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin.UI --no-dependencies`, `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin --no-dependencies`, `dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-dependencies`: 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) each (TreatWarningsAsErrors clean). `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-build`: Failed 0, Passed 162, Skipped 0, Total 162, 22 s. Nothing was modified; the progress file was not written; no other package's files were touched.

HOST RUN — Wakeel.Admin.exe launched with --remote-debugging-port=9334 --window-size=1366x768 and a fresh temporary --data-folder; /json/version answered (Edg 153); every screenshot taken at exactly 1366x768 through Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride and looked at. I drove the whole package myself rather than trusting the builder's run: A01 (password + names → recovery sheet: one 21-character code Y85S-3N20-359K-63E8-ZGGPK plus QR, no «تذكر هذا الجهاز», acknowledgement → «ابدأ») → A03 → A05 (دائرة الشؤون الإدارية / قسم الصادر والوارد / وحدة الأرشيف المركزي, marked an office with code INV-1042; a unit's detail pane offers no fifth-layer «إضافة …», so the four fixed levels hold) → A06 (three devices, the three roles, both scopes, numbers 1-3) → A07 (office key issued, two accounts activated, الجهاز ٢ revoked through the typed danger dialog → signed revocation list) → A04 (logo uploaded through the hidden InputFile, letter template read) → back to A03. Both themes: the appearance switch correctly offered «المظهر الفاتح» while the page was dark, and every screen was screenshotted dark and light beside its A-preview. Host log after the whole run: one line, «Wakeel admin host starting up», no WRN/ERR/FTL. Process killed and the endpoint confirmed silent.

VISUAL FIDELITY (host beside design/exports/preview/{dark,light}/A) — A04: same two-by-two grid, اسم الهيئة | شعار الهيئة on the first row, الدورة المالية | صيغة ترقيم الملفات on the second, قالب التقرير الشهري full width below, amber item-5 caution inside the card. The round-1 high is genuinely fixed: the nine placeholder marks are WChip (Success/Warning/Neutral) in a plain `<ul>`, and the three file choosers are real WButtons over an out-of-sight InputFile opened by wakeelAdmin.openFilePicker. The A4 sheet renders as a letter with the letterhead once (mc:Fallback regression holds). A05: one detail card with «المكتب والجرد» folded in as a section; deviations from the preview (four fields two to a row instead of six three to a row, no «التحقق من صحة الهيكل» panel, no node-count badge or Ctrl+F hint) are outside B1-A05 and stand under the specification-wins ruling; the flat tree is the one reserved deviation. A06: same anatomy as the preview — offices rail with search and counts, office header with path and the inventory-code chip on the far side, devices table, the information banner and the «آخر تحديث» foot line the round-1 low asked for; measured `.w-table-scroll` scrollWidth 1004 vs clientWidth 959 but with `overflow: visible` nothing spills or scrolls on screen — the table sits inside its card in both themes, so the round-1 medium is closed in effect. A07: `.w-table-scroll` 948/929 and 181/172, again no visible bar; key card, revocation list and accounts table all present and aligned; the row action icons are right-aligned within their cell, so the extra «تفعيل» button on a pending row does not break the column. The one visible A07 deviation from its preview is finding 1 — the preview shows «تراجع» live beside a dimmed confirm, the host dims both.

SECURITY — checked on the live data folder. admin.db has no SQLite header (SQLCipher); greps for the administrator password, the recovery code and the administrator/employee names return nothing. logs/wakeel-admin-20260917.log holds one INF line and no secret. keys/revocations.json holds device ids, instants, the org id and an Ed25519 signature only. keys/admin.key holds the administrator name and wrapped database keys, no clear key material. ui-state.json holds {"theme":"light"}. Device seeds are sealed with the database key at issue time, zeroed in a finally (Array.Clear on both seeds and the serialized copy), handed out exactly once by TakeSeedsForExport which nulls the column in the same call and returns SeedsAlreadyExported on a second take, and wiped again on revoke — and A07 now correctly distinguishes the three fates (verified live: الجهاز ٢ revoked before any export reads «أُتلفت بذرة المفتاح عند إلغاء الجهاز»). The office key is RandomBytes(32), sealed with the database key, zeroed after sealing, and only ever leaves wrapped to the device's own X25519 key under a fixed context. Revocation lists are signed by the organisation identity. The letter template is parsed as a zip with XDocument (DTDs prohibited by default, no macro execution); the report template is now checked structurally for word/document.xml instead of by its name; the logo is validated by PNG/JPEG header, ≤ 2 MB, ≥ 48px. The square crop now really exists and works: AdminWindowsImageSquareCrop is registered in App.xaml.cs before AddWakeelAdmin and turned my 600×300 PNG into a 300×300 square with the focus slider rendered and re-cropping live.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS — of the fourteen, thirteen are genuinely closed (verified in code and, where visible, on the host): the five hand-rolled chip families and the fake button, both table scroll defects, the false seed wording, the missing square crop, the Latin figures in Arabic prose, «جهازان نشطان», the report-template structure check, the inspector's own MaxBytes, the COALESCE in ReadDeviceRow, the CouldNotSave refusal, the revoked-row tooltips, the A06 banner and foot line, the A05 fold, and A01's footer hint. The fourteenth — the invisible confirmation gate — was fixed for the confirm button and broken for the cancel button in the same rule (finding 1). The six deferred admin-1 lows are closed in code.

TESTS — the assertions are real behaviour, not tautologies: the structure suite drives the level rules, sibling-name rules, move loops, branch disable, delete refusals and office-code uniqueness through the service and reads the result back out of the database; the key suite issues certificates and verifies them against the organisation key and the whole chain, proves seeds can be taken once, proves a revoked certificate is turned away by the chain check, and proves the rotated office key wraps per device; the organisation suite covers the letterhead regression, the misspelt-mark case, IsWordDocument against a real zip without a document part, and the inspector's own size limit; the four Counting.ActiveDevices shapes are asserted individually. The one weak spot is the danger-dialog test, which asserts a marker class rather than the rendered state — which is precisely why finding 1 passed unnoticed.

ARABIC / RTL — user-facing text is Arabic throughout, no technical terms, no error codes, no mention of servers, ports, internet or PostgreSQL anywhere on the four screens. All five icon-only buttons on A06/A07 carry tooltips, and a switched-off one now says why it is off. Latin and numeric tokens (INV-1042, docx, dates, YYYYMMDD/DESSS) are wrapped in Bdi, and the three pages set `unicode-bidi: plaintext` on shared component titles. The two remaining Arabic-language defects are findings 5 and 9.

WHAT BLOCKS ACCEPTANCE — one high (the locked danger dialog also switches off «العودة», leaving no visible way back out of the tool's irreversible-action dialogs) and two mediums (the A04 crop slider's toast-and-write storm on every drag step, and the hand-rolled offices rail on A06). The A05 tree is recorded once as the reserved deviation and is not held against the package.
